contract: the rendering fixtures whose libass result C leaves to the target, rendered and folded as ass-render renders and folds them: libass's renderer overflows int or converts a double out of int's range on the way to the result (a horizontal border beyond 2^30 frame pixels doubled in int for the width of an event's box; an event box taller than int holds, whose collision boxes end up 2^31 or more rows apart, where cmp_rect_y0's int subtraction wraps and glibc's merge sort orders them)

each case is pinned per target from that target's own reference run; a case passes when the candidate, the reference and the target's pin agree, and a target a case has no pin for runs and reports it without comparing

the renderer follows libass built with GCC for 32-bit ARM hard-float: an int overflow wraps and a conversion out of int's range saturates; where libass for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu gives another result, the case is open there as a deliberate divergence

the fixture and its attached font files are read before each timed and memory operation, which, as a player does, creates the library, hands it the attached fonts (ass_add_font copies them; the candidate copies them into its budget), opens the default font file (libass through FreeType; the candidate reads it), creates and configures the renderer, reads the script or runs the stream and renders every frame; the timed span is the reading and the rendering, on both sides: it starts once the renderer is configured, since each libass setter empties the renderer's caches (ass_reconfigure), and ends before the track, renderer and library are freed, so neither side times a cache reset or the teardown; libass opens the default font file when a glyph first needs it, inside the span, and the candidate reads it before

timing and memory are measured against libass-player-native, libass.a linked as a player links it with none of its sources compiled into the worker; the parity reference libass-ass-native compiles libass's rendering, drawing and parsing sources with checks that note the conversions C leaves to the target, and is never timed or measured
pending_module_requirements: a deliberate divergence: libass built with GCC for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu converts an event box's top, height, left and width from double to int with vector instructions that keep the low 32 bits (ass_render.c:2995-3003), where 32-bit ARM saturates, so it also loses the box of a BorderStyle 4 event whose vertical border exceeds 2^30 frame pixels and moves events colliding with such a border elsewhere; the renderer follows libass on 32-bit ARM with GCC
